Stage 1G merged: PAdES B-B to B-LTA sealing, self-verified, agreeing with pyHanko and EU DSS ( T-1G ). Stage 1I merged: hash-chained audit trail, RFC 8785, Merkle anchoring, certificate of completion with the trail embedded ( T-1I ). Reader completion merged: password-protected PDFs (standard handler R2–R6), LZW, four wrongly refused real PDFs fixed, a public content lexer; 417 of 422 corpus PDFs open ( PDF-ENC-01 , PDF-LZW-01 , PDF-REAL-01..03 ). Stage 1E merged: flattening with subset fonts, drawn, uploaded and typed signatures, and fill-in-place forms ( T-1E , FILL-01 ), checked by PDFium a

Hostile PDF fixtures: generator and manifest covering every PDF limit in docs/21 ( F-005 ). Real-world PDF corpus: a manifest of 422 freely licensed PDFs (URL, SHA-256, licence, producer, features), a fetch script that checks them and a byte scanner that describes them ( fixtures/corpus , F-004 ). Envelope-centric REST API ( docs/40 ). Errors are RFC 9457 problem details with a stable code ( docs/20 ) and a request_id . Every POST accepts Idempotency-Key ; replays within 24 hours return the first response. Envelopes carry an ETag ( "v<version>" ); edits of drafts and corrections need If-Match . Lists page with cursor and limit . Times are RFC 3339 UTC; ids are UUIDv7. Objects of another account answer exactly as missing ones: 404 CS-API-0002 . The /s/{token} endpoints are the recipient ceremony, not public API ( docs/40 ). Authentication: bearer : A personal API key ( osk_… ) or an acce

Run the whole OpenSeal stack on one machine with Docker Compose, create the first administrator, and send yourself a document to sign. About ten minutes, most of it the first image build. A development stack. It generates its own certificate authority, keeps the seal key in a software HSM and runs a local timestamp authority, so its seals validate only against that generated root, not in Adobe Acrobat. OpenSeal is pre-alpha: do not use it for real agreements yet.

Docker with Compose v2 (Docker Desktop, or Docker Engine with the compose plugin). Git, and a few gigabytes of free disk for the images. Ports 8080 and 8025 free on 127.0.0.1 (both can be moved, see below).

Clone the repository and start everything. --wait returns once every service reports healthy. git clone https://github.com/CasualOffice/openseal cd openseal docker compose up -d --build --wait On the first start a one-shot pki service writes a development CA, the TLS certificates between services, the seal key and certificate, a timestamp certificate, the API token key and random passwords into a secrets volume. Nothing secret is baked into an image.

An install starts empty. bootstrap creates the first account and its administrator, and prints their ids. Run it once; a second run with the same email is refused. docker compose exec -e OPENSEAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD='a long passphrase' server \ casual-sign-server bootstrap "Acme" admin@acme.example "Ada Admin"

Open the web app at http://localhost:8080 and sign in as admin@acme.example with the passphrase you chose. Choose Start , then drop a PDF on the page. Add a signer with any email address, place a signature and a date field, and send. Sending your first envelope walks through each step. Open Mailpit at http://localhost:8025 . Every email the stack sends lands there, including the signing invitation. Follow the link in the invitation, consent, and sign. When the last signer finishes, the worker seals the document and both the sealed PDF and its certificate of completion appear on the envelope. T

To see the web app without Docker, serve it in demo mode. Data lives only in the browser tab; nothing is sent or signed. python3 -I tools/serve-webapp.py # open http://127.0.0.1:8130/app.html?mock=1 # sign in as demo@openseal.test with the password openseal-demo-1

Service What it does server The API, the signing ceremony and the web app, on port 8080 worker Email through Mailpit, reminders and expiry, sealing through keyd and the timestamp authority, webhooks keyd The key daemon over mutual TLS; the seal key in a SoftHSM token postgres The database; the application role is bound by row-level security migrate One-shot: applies every migration before the server starts s3 An S3-compatible blob store (SeaweedFS) for documents mailpit Catches all email; web UI on port 8025 tsa A development RFC 3161 timestamp authority pki One-shot, first start only: the dev

docker compose logs -f server worker # what it is doing docker compose down # stop, keep the data docker compose down -v # stop and discard every volume (data, keys, mail) Ports bind to 127.0.0.1 only. Set OPENSEAL_HTTP_PORT (default 8080) or OPENSEAL_MAIL_PORT (default 8025) to move them.

Download the sealed PDF from the envelope, then fetch the stack's root certificate and check the seal with the browser verifier or any PAdES validator: docker compose exec -T keyd cat /secrets/ca.pem > openseal-dev-root.pem Open http://localhost:8080/verify.html , add openseal-dev-root.pem as a trusted certificate and drop the PDF. A PAdES seal with a trusted timestamp, a certificate of completion and the audit trail inside the PDF. Evidence first

A completed agreement shows which document every party saw, who signed it, when and how. Anyone can check that for decades, with no account and no server. PAdES B-T by default, up to B-LTA Sealed as an incremental update with an RFC 3161 timestamp. Long-term validation and archive renewal are one setting away. Hash-chained audit trail Every event is canonical JSON (RFC 8785) linked by SHA-256 to the one before it. Deleting, inserting, reordering or editing any event is detected. Checked by independent validators Our verifier, pyHanko and EU DSS must agree on every sealed and tampered fixture;

Nothing calls home. server : the API, the signing ceremony and the web app worker : email, reminders, sealing and webhooks keyd : the seal key behind PKCS#11, over mutual TLS PostgreSQL : row-level security per account S3-compatible store : write-once documents Timestamp authority : a development TSA, or yours Self-hosting guide # Build and start everything git clone https://github.com/CasualOffice/openseal cd openseal docker compose up -d --build --wait # Create the first account and administrator docker compose exec \ -e

Every serious open-source e-signature project is AGPL, which most companies cannot ship inside their products. OpenSeal can go anywhere. Use it in SaaS, on-premises, desktop and mobile products. No royalties and no separate commercial licence. Fork it, rename it, sell what you build. Keep the LICENSE and NOTICE when you redistribute it. OpenSeal never adds its name to your application or to the PDFs it produces. Powered by OpenSeal A credit like this is appreciated, never required. Logos and snippets

More in the documentation FAQ . Can I use it for real agreements today? Not yet. OpenSeal is pre-alpha: the engine is complete and tested, and the server and web app run end to end on Docker Compose, but the release gates (an external security review, an accessibility audit, validation in Adobe Acrobat and a counsel review) are still ahead. The roadmap shows what is left for Release 1. Are the signatures legally binding? OpenSeal is designed to support electronic-signature laws such as ESIGN, UETA and eIDAS.
